items.title: The Intoxicated owl
items.dimensions_notes:
Size: 75 x 65 cm. 
Type: Framed
Acrylic on paper.
items.description: The Intoxicated Owl is a whimsical imaginary artwork inspired by the mysterious charm of owls, creatures often associated with wisdom, curiosity, and quiet observation across many cultures. This piece captures an owl in a dreamy, intoxicated state, balancing humor with personality and atmosphere. The carefully chosen color palette allows the artwork to complement a wide variety of interior spaces, adding character and presence to any wall. The artwork is completely original and created entirely from imagination, without copying or using references from existing artworks or images found online. Its concept, composition, and character are uniquely developed as an independent creative expression. Created to spark imagination and conversation, this painting carries a playful yet thoughtful energy that invites viewers to pause, observe, and interpret it in their own way.

items.title: Soul in Soil
items.dimensions_notes:
Size: 75 x 65 cm. 
Type: Unframed
Acrylic on paper.
items.description: This painting reflects what it truly means to be human — a being shaped from dust, living on the same earth, bound to time, nature, and the unseen force that sustains all existence. On the left, the wooden clock holds Roman, Arabic, and Hindi numbers — three voices from three eras. Roman echoes a language long gone, Arabic stands as an ancient tongue still alive, and Hindi represents the young pulse of the present. Together, they show how time moves through civilizations while remaining unchanged in its silent flow. At the center sits a faceless human. The absence of a face allows every viewer to find themselves within this figure. Humanity is not defined by intellect, but by our simple origin: shaped from earth, fed by earth, dependent on its plants, waters, and creatures — and sustained by the One who created us from dust. The roots above symbolize ancestry and the weight of all that came before us. The blue water below represents life — ever-moving and ever-returning. The vines, flowers, and small creatures show how nature nurtures us even when we forget our beginnings. The single flower in the figure's hand becomes a gesture of gratitude and awareness of the intelligent designer in all creation. This artwork is a reminder that no matter where we go — we remain dust, carried by time, and sustained by the same Source that breathed life into us.

items.title: Invention of Toilet in Stone Age
items.dimensions_notes:
Size: 75 x 65 cm. 
Type: Unframed
Oil pastels on paper.
items.description: The Invention of Toilet in the Stone Age is a completely original imaginary artwork created entirely from imagination. The concept explores a humorous and thought-provoking vision of what the invention of a toilet might have looked like if it had existed during the Stone Age. The painting features various primitive elements associated with early human civilization, including stone tools, raw meat, handmade weapons, hut-like shelters, and expressive characters reacting with surprise and curiosity toward the unusual invention before them. Blending comedy, creativity, and storytelling, the artwork creates a playful contrast between ancient human life and modern ideas. Every element in the composition is uniquely designed as an independent creative expression and is not copied or recreated from existing artworks or online references. With its detailed atmosphere and imaginative concept, this piece adds character, conversation, and artistic energy to any interior space while standing as a distinctive example of original creative art.
